reason: E2 directly shows that Mo increases strength but reduces toughness, and that Nb has a minor effect on strength while improving ductility, supporting the first two premises. The remaining premises about electronegativity, lattice strain, and dislocation mobility are mechanistic inferences not directly evidenced in the cited passages, and the retention of BCC structure is assumed rather than shown.
premises: Mo increases yield strength but reduces toughness in refractory HEAs
Nb decreases yield strength only slightly and improves ductility in refractory HEAs
Reducing Mo content lowers electronegativity difference and lattice strain
Lower electronegativity difference and lattice strain enhance dislocation mobility and plasticity
Partial Mo-to-Nb substitution retains a disordered BCC structure under identical processing
